messages:
lisa: Hi team — need help. I finalized a divorce on 2026-02-15 but only just realized my spouse is still on my Redwood medical plan. Can I remove them retroactively and get a premium refund? What docs do you need?

jamie-hr: sorry to hear that, lisa. short answer: likely yes, but we need the life event submitted + supporting docs. Redwood policy usually requires life event changes within 30 days of the event, but we can make exceptions for documented cases. please submit the life event in Workday first.

hr-bot: Automated reminder — submit a "Life Event: Change in Marital Status" in Workday: https://redwood.workday.com -> Benefits > Report Life Event. Attach documentation to the life event case.

lisa: thanks — i submitted the life event and uploaded the divorce decree and final judgment PDF. (case 68241)

chris-peopleops: got it, looking. two quick Qs: 1) were any premium subsidies applied (employer HSA/FSAs or pre-tax)? 2) is the ex-spouse covered under another plan now? both affect whether we owe a refund vs. eligibility for COBRA.

lisa: 1) no HSA employer contribution this month. 2) not that i know of. ex-spouse was on my plan and said they would find their own coverage.

marta-payroll: payroll note — if we approve a retro removal we typically process a premium adjustment in the next payroll cycle and any refund/credit is issued as a payroll adjustment within 1–2 cycles. if the change affects FSA/HSA pretax elections we may need to reconcile contributions with benefits carrier — that can add an extra cycle.

jamie-hr: next steps for you, lisa: 1) confirm the Workday life event has your divorce decree attached. 2) email benefits@redwood.com with your employee ID and the life event case number (68241) and request retroactive removal to the divorce date (2026-02-15). 3) note whether you want any refunded premium as payroll credit or direct deposit. we'll review and reply within 3–5 business days.

alex: quick follow-up — for domestic partnerships we accept a signed termination affidavit or same docs (court order) depending on the state. if anyone else is in a similar situation, ping us before uploading to make sure you attach the right doc type.

lisa: pinged benefits@redwood.com with case number and asked for payroll credit. thanks. :heart:

jamie-hr: confirmed receipt. we'll route to benefits admin and loop in marta for payroll action. if approved, benefits admin will update the coverage effective date to 2026-02-15 and notify the carrier; payroll will do retro adjustment.

marta-payroll: noted — if carrier accepts the retro effective date we will process premium refund as payroll adjustment on next cycle (target within 2 cycles). if carrier rejects retro coverage, we will follow their guidance and provide options (e.g., COBRA notices).

chris-peopleops: FYI for records — tagging this as "exception life event" for audit. we'll keep the evidence in the benefits case.

lisa: appreciated. any chance you can confirm once the carrier accepts? i need to know if ex will be eligible for COBRA.

jamie-hr: will do. benefits admin will confirm carrier response and whether COBRA needs to be offered — we typically send COBRA election packets if coverage is terminated for a dependent due to divorce. expect an update in this thread once carrier responds. :+1:
